```{r fig3-build}
# height proportional to its 5 rows and keeps ONE shared x axis and one tag.
BLOCKS <- c("Per-OTU niche", "Guild mean")   # short: the lower block is only 5 rows tall
otu_df <- data.frame(lab = sel$lab, Guild = sel$Guild, resolved = sel$resolved,
                     est = sel$beta_season_mean,
                     lo = sel$beta_season_CrI2.5, hi = sel$beta_season_CrI97.5,
                     block = factor(BLOCKS[1], levels = BLOCKS))
gm_df  <- data.frame(lab = gm$lab, Guild = gm$Guild, est = gm$mean,
                     lo = gm$q25, hi = gm$q75,
                     block = factor(BLOCKS[2], levels = BLOCKS))
lvl <- c(gm_df$lab[order(gm_df$est)], otu_df$lab[order(otu_df$est)])
otu_df$lab <- factor(otu_df$lab, levels = lvl)
gm_df$lab  <- factor(gm_df$lab,  levels = lvl)

# Convergence is checked here but PRINTED IN THE CAPTION, not on the panel: a
# diagnostic belongs in the caption rather than on the face of a main-text
# figure. The guard refuses to draw the figure from a fit that does not meet
# the Section 9.1 criteria (every Beta PSRF < 1.1; chains agree on the guild
# means and the variance partition to within 0.05).
conv <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "hmsc_convergence_psrf.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cclr <- conv[conv$model == "clr", ]
stopifnot(nrow(cclr) == 1L, cclr$beta_psrf_max < 1.1, cclr$beta_pct_below_1.1 == 100,
          cclr$guild_mean_chain_range_max < 0.05, cclr$vp_chain_range_max < 0.05)
n_ci <- sum(b$beta_season_CrI2.5 > 0 | b$beta_season_CrI97.5 < 0)
stopifnot(n_ci == 74L)

# OTU1369's credible interval reaches below -6; drawn in full it would widen
# the axis for one row. Intervals are therefore clipped at +/- 6 and the
# clipped end carries an arrowhead, so nothing is hidden: the reader sees that
# the interval continues, and the caption says how far.
XCLIP <- 6
otu_df$lo_c <- pmax(otu_df$lo, -XCLIP)
otu_df$hi_c <- pmin(otu_df$hi,  XCLIP)
otu_df$lo_clip <- otu_df$lo < -XCLIP
otu_df$hi_clip <- otu_df$hi >  XCLIP
n_clip <- sum(otu_df$lo_clip | otu_df$hi_clip)
# Nothing may be clipped so hard that its point estimate leaves the panel.
stopifnot(all(abs(otu_df$est) < XCLIP), all(abs(gm_df$est) < XCLIP),
          all(abs(c(gm_df$lo, gm_df$hi)) < XCLIP))
arr <- grid::arrow(length = unit(0.055, "in"), type = "open", angle = 22)

pA <- ggplot(otu_df, aes(est, lab, colour = Guild)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey70") +
  # geom_segment rather than geom_errorbarh: the latter is deprecated in
  # ggplot2 4.0 and its replacement's argument names differ between versions.
  geom_segment(aes(x = lo_c, xend = hi_c, y = lab, yend = lab), linewidth = 0.45, alpha = 0.75) +
  # Arrowheads drawn as short overlays at the clipped ends rather than as an
  # arrow on the main segment, so an interval clipped at BOTH ends still gets
  # two heads and an unclipped one gets none.
  geom_segment(data = otu_df[otu_df$hi_clip, ],
               aes(x = XCLIP - 0.30, xend = XCLIP, y = lab, yend = lab),
               linewidth = 0.45, alpha = 0.75, arrow = arr) +
  geom_segment(data = otu_df[otu_df$lo_clip, ],
               aes(x = -XCLIP + 0.30, xend = -XCLIP, y = lab, yend = lab),
               linewidth = 0.45, alpha = 0.75, arrow = arr) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = resolved), size = 2.3, stroke = 0.8) +
  # guild block: IQR segment behind, mean diamond on top, value printed
  geom_segment(data = gm_df, aes(x = lo, xend = hi, y = lab, yend = lab),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey65", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = gm_df, aes(est, lab, fill = Guild), inherit.aes = FALSE,
             shape = 23, size = 3.2, colour = "grey20", stroke = 0.4) +
  # Value printed to the RIGHT of the IQR, not above the diamond: the five guild
  # means sit within 0.6 of each other, so a label above one row lands on the next.
  geom_text(data = gm_df, aes(hi, lab, label = sprintf("%+.2f", est)), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.10, size = 2.9, colour = "grey20") +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(block), scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = guild_cols, name = "Guild", drop = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = guild_cols, guide = "none", drop = FALSE) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Posterior support >= 0.95" = 16, "Not resolved" = 1),
                     name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-6, 6, 2), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.09))) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-XCLIP, XCLIP)) +
  labs(x = "HMSC Beta: Season (CLR abundance, positive = more abundant in summer)", y = NULL,
       subtitle = sprintf(paste0("The %d OTUs holding >= %.0f%% of modelled read share each (%.0f%% of modelled reads).\n",
                                 "Abundance (CLR) model; %d of %d resolved at 0.95 posterior support."),
                          nrow(sel), 100 * SHARE_MIN, 100 * sel_cov, n_res, nrow(sel))) +
  base_theme +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_markdown(size = 8.5),
        strip.placement = "outside",
        strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 90, face = "bold", size = 8)) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(shape = 16, size = 2.6)),
         shape  = guide_legend(order = 2))

# ============================================================================
# Panel B -- variance partition (CLR), community-wide and by guild
# ============================================================================
vp <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "hmsc_variance_partition.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
# Components are stored rounded to 4 dp, so a row sums to 1 only to within the
# rounding error of three values -- hence 1e-3 rather than machine tolerance.
stopifnot(nrow(vp) == 226L, setequal(vp$OTU_ID, b$OTU_ID),
          all(VP_LEVELS %in% names(vp)),
          max(abs(rowSums(vp[, VP_LEVELS]) - 1)) < 1e-3)
vp$Guild <- factor(unname(guild_map[vp$guild]), levels = GUILD_LEVELS)

# Row order and emphasis are EDITORIAL, not statistical: the community row and
# the two guilds this study is about are drawn larger and grouped at the top so
# the panel states its point before the reader parses six bars. The caption says
# this explicitly, because pathotrophs -- de-emphasised here -- actually carry
# the largest Season share of any guild.
ROW_ORDER <- c("All modelled OTUs", "Dung saprotroph", "Unassigned / dark",
               "Plant-associated", "Pathotroph", "Other assigned")
EMPH <- c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)

grp_mean <- function(d, label) data.frame(
  grp = label, n = nrow(d), t(colMeans(d[, VP_LEVELS])), check.names = FALSE)
vpm <- rbind(grp_mean(vp, ROW_ORDER[1]),
             do.call(rbind, lapply(ROW_ORDER[-1],
                                   function(g) grp_mean(vp[vp$Guild == g, ], g))))
stopifnot(identical(vpm$grp, ROW_ORDER), vpm$n[1] == 226L, sum(vpm$n[-1]) == 226L)
# Drift guard: the community means are quoted in Section 9.2, Table S-HMSCc and
# the caption.
VP_EXP <- c(Season = 31.53, Year = 18.55, `Random: sample` = 49.93)
stopifnot(max(abs(100 * unlist(vpm[1, VP_LEVELS], use.names = FALSE) -
                  VP_EXP[VP_LEVELS])) < 0.05)

# PCR-replicate share, MODEL-FREE (Section 9.2, Table S-HMSCc2): replicate-to-
# replicate variance of CLR within a dropping as a share of that OTU's total
# CLR variance, averaged over OTUs. It is NOT a fourth component of the bar:
# the bar partitions the model's explained variance, this is a share of TOTAL
# variance, so it is drawn as a separate column and the caption says so.
pcr <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "hmsc_pcr_replicate_variance.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
pcr_lab <- c(all = "All modelled OTUs", guild_map)
stopifnot(setequal(pcr$group, names(pcr_lab)))
vpm$pcr_share <- pcr$share_total_mean[match(vpm$grp, unname(pcr_lab[pcr$group]))]
stopifnot(!anyNA(vpm$pcr_share), abs(vpm$pcr_share[1] - 0.324) < 0.001)

# Manual geometry on a CONTINUOUS y axis. A discrete axis spaces rows evenly
# whatever width the bars are given, so it cannot produce "larger and grouped at
# the top"; here each row carries its own height and its own gap below it.
H_EMPH <- 0.82; H_MIN <- 0.46
GAP    <- c(0.90, 0.45, 0.70, 0.40, 0.40, 0.00)   # space BELOW each row
vpm$h   <- ifelse(EMPH, H_EMPH, H_MIN)
vpm$emph <- EMPH
edge <- 0
ctr  <- numeric(nrow(vpm))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(vpm))) {
  ctr[i] <- edge - vpm$h[i] / 2
  edge   <- edge - vpm$h[i] - GAP[i]
}
vpm$ctr <- ctr
sep_y <- ctr[1] - vpm$h[1] / 2 - GAP[1] / 2       # rule under the community row

# Stacking done by hand (cumsum), not position_stack: the label layers below
# plot a different set of rows than the bars, and position_stack re-stacks
# whatever data it is handed, so the two would silently drift apart.
rect <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(vpm)), function(i) {
  v <- 100 * unlist(vpm[i, VP_LEVELS], use.names = FALSE)
  data.frame(comp = factor(unname(vp_display[VP_LEVELS]),
                           levels = unname(vp_display[VP_LEVELS])),
             xmin = cumsum(c(0, head(v, -1))), xmax = cumsum(v),
             ymin = vpm$ctr[i] - vpm$h[i] / 2, ymax = vpm$ctr[i] + vpm$h[i] / 2)
}))

# Season is the one segment whose exact value the reader needs; print it inside.
slab <- data.frame(x = 100 * vpm$Season / 2, y = vpm$ctr,
                   txt = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * vpm$Season),
                   sz  = ifelse(EMPH, 3.3, 2.7))
tot  <- data.frame(x = 103, y = vpm$ctr,
                   txt = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (vpm$Season + vpm$Year)),
                   sz  = ifelse(EMPH, 3.2, 2.8))
X_PCR <- 121                                          # model-free column, right of a divider
pcrt <- data.frame(x = X_PCR, y = vpm$ctr,
                   txt = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * vpm$pcr_share),
                   sz  = ifelse(EMPH, 3.2, 2.8))
y_top <- vpm$ctr[1] + vpm$h[1] / 2
hdr  <- data.frame(x = c(106, X_PCR + 3.5), y = y_top + 0.25,   # centred over each column
                   txt = c("Season\n+ Year", "PCR rep.\n(model-free)"))
ylab <- ifelse(vpm$emph,
               sprintf("<span style='font-size:10.5pt'>**%s**</span><br>(n = %d)", vpm$grp, vpm$n),
               sprintf("<span style='font-size:8.5pt'>%s</span><br>(n = %d)", vpm$grp, vpm$n))

pB <- ggplot(rect) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = comp),
            colour = "white", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = sep_y, colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(data = slab, aes(x, y, label = txt, size = sz), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            colour = "white", fontface = "bold") +
  geom_text(data = tot, aes(x, y, label = txt, size = sz), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = 0, colour = "grey25") +
  # model-free column: divider + italic values, visibly not part of the bar
  annotate("segment", x = 116, xend = 116, y = min(vpm$ctr - vpm$h / 2), yend = y_top,
           colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "22") +
  geom_text(data = pcrt, aes(x, y, label = txt, size = sz), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = 0, colour = "grey35", fontface = "italic") +
  geom_text(data = hdr, aes(x, y, label = txt), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0, size = 2.6, colour = "grey35", lineheight = 0.9) +
  scale_size_identity() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = vp_cols, name = "Variance component") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25), limits = c(0, 136),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0)),
                     labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = vpm$ctr, labels = ylab, expand = expansion(add = c(0.18, 0.75))) +
  labs(x = "Mean share of per-OTU variance", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "Abundance (CLR) model, PCR replicates averaged;\nall 226 OTUs, then by guild.") +
  base_theme +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_markdown(size = 8.5, lineheight = 1.1, colour = "grey15"),
        axis.line.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank()) +
  # cap the x axis line at the bar's 0-100% range so the text columns to its
  # right do not read as part of the scale
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1), x = guide_axis(cap = "both"))

# ---- assemble and write ----------------------------------------------------
fig3 <- (pA | pB) +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.25, 1), guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  # VERIFIED the hard way: the three collected key blocks (guild, support,
  # variance component) do NOT fit side by side at 11 in -- legend.box =
  # "horizontal" overflows the device and is silently clipped, with no warning.
  # They are stacked instead, and each is forced onto a single row so the block
  # costs three text lines rather than four.
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical",
        legend.box.just = "left", legend.margin = margin(t = 0, b = 0),
        legend.box.spacing = unit(0.25, "cm"))

# Every main figure is written three ways: PNG and JPG (600 dpi raster, for
# submission systems that demand one or the other) and PDF (vector, for print).
save_fig <- function(stem, obj, width, height, res = 600) {
  one <- function(open_dev) { open_dev(); on.exit(grDevices::dev.off()); print(obj) }
  one(function() grDevices::png(paste0(stem, ".png"), width = width, height = height,
                                units = "in", res = res))
  one(function() grDevices::jpeg(paste0(stem, ".jpg"), width = width, height = height,
                                 units = "in", res = res, quality = 95))
  pdf_dev <- if (capabilities("cairo")) grDevices::cairo_pdf else grDevices::pdf
  one(function() pdf_dev(paste0(stem, ".pdf"), width = width, height = height))
}
save_fig(file.path(out_dir, "Fig3_hmsc_synthesis"), fig3, 11.5, 6.4)

# ---- console summary -------------------------------------------------------
cat(sprintf("Panel A: %d OTUs at >= %.0f%% modelled read share each = %.1f%% of modelled reads.\n",
            nrow(sel), 100 * SHARE_MIN, 100 * sel_cov))
cat(sprintf("Resolved: %d of %d at 0.95 posterior support (%d at the winter end); %d of %d OTUs community-wide have a 95%% CrI excluding 0.\n",
            n_res, nrow(sel), sum(sel$resolved == "Posterior support >= 0.95" &
                                  sel$beta_season_mean < 0), n_ci, nrow(b)))
cat(sprintf("CLR convergence (caption): Beta median PSRF %.2f, %.0f%% of parameters < 1.1.\n",
            cclr$beta_psrf_med, cclr$beta_pct_below_1.1))
cat(sprintf("Credible intervals clipped at +/-%.1f (arrowed): %d of %d.\n",
            XCLIP, n_clip, nrow(otu_df)))
cat("\nPanel A rows, summer end first:\n")
print(data.frame(OTU = sel$OTU_ID, label = gsub("\\*", "", sel$lab),
                 guild = as.character(sel$Guild),
                 beta = round(sel$beta_season_mean, 2),
                 support = sel$beta_season_support,
                 read_pct = round(100 * sel$rel, 2)), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nGuild means over all 226 OTUs:\n")
print(data.frame(guild = as.character(gm$Guild), n = gm$n,
                 mean_beta = round(gm$mean, 3),
                 IQR = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", gm$q25, gm$q75)), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nVariance partition (mean % per OTU):\n")
print(data.frame(group = sprintf("%s (n = %d)", vpm$grp, vpm$n),
                 round(100 * vpm[, VP_LEVELS], 1), check.names = FALSE),
      row.names = FALSE)
```

### 10.4 Figure 4 — Richness rises, evenness collapses (H2)

:::: {.content-visible when-profile="docs"}
*Provenance: Fig. 4A is the coverage-based pooled-season iNEXT3D analysis of Section 5.1 (Table S8); Fig. 4B the size-standardised per-sample iNEXT3D Hill numbers of Section 5.2 (Figure S8), annotated with the per-sample gamma-GLM contrasts of Table S9; Fig. 4C the dominance and evenness metrics of Section 5.3 (Table S10); Fig. 4D the top-5 dominant OTUs of Section 5.4 (Table S11), coloured by the guild rule of Section 8.1. Panels B–D are computed on the canonical 52-sample object (`alldat$nopool`); panel B standardises it to 12,615 reads through the shared `hill_size_helper.R`, the same single source Section 5.2 uses. Panel A's estimates and every test statistic are read from the committed `tables/` CSVs, so the figure cannot drift from Section 5.*
::::

![](figures/main/Fig4_richness_evenness_crossover.png)

**Figure 4**: The summer dung mycobiome is the richer assemblage when droppings are pooled, yet each individual dropping is far less even. **(A)** Taxonomic diversity of each season's pooled sample set at Hill orders q = 0, 1 and 2, at equal sequencing depth (every sample rarefied to 12,615 reads) and equal sample coverage (0.65) (iNEXT3D, incidence data); points are the median estimate over 50 rarefaction draws, bars the median 95% confidence interval, and the grey segment joins the two seasons within an order. Summer exceeds winter at every order (Table S8). **(B)** Per-sample Hill numbers for the same 52 samples, size-standardised with iNEXT3D to a common depth of 12,615 reads, drawn in the same three columns against the same season axis so that the two rows can be read against one another; boxes show the median and interquartile range, points are individual samples, white diamonds are season means, and the grey segment joins those means. The slope that rises in all three columns of (A) rises only at q = 0 here and falls at q = 1 and q = 2 — that reversal is the crossover. Annotations give the year-adjusted summer/winter ratio and its p-value from a gamma GLM fitted to the plotted per-sample values (Table S9); the q = 0 contrast depends on the model family (p = 0.026–0.29; Table S9b), the q = 1 and q = 2 contrasts do not. Both rows scale y freely within each column, because the three Hill orders differ by an order of magnitude. **(C)** The mechanism: per-sample top-1-OTU read share and Pielou evenness *J*, both on a 0–1 scale, with symbols as in (B) and brackets giving the Wilcoxon rank-sum result (Table S10). **(D)** The identity of the dominants — the five OTUs with the highest mean within-season read share in each season, coloured by functional guild under the rule of Section 8.1. Bar labels give that mean share and, in parentheses, the number of the season's 26 samples in which the OTU was detected at all. Taxa are named at the finest confidently assigned rank, so an OTU with no genus appears under its family, or as *unclassified* plus its order or class. *Candida parapsilosis* is coloured plant-associated because its compound FUNGuild string contains `Epiphyte`; the rule is applied unchanged rather than special-cased, so that Figures 1 and 4 and Sections 8–9 classify every OTU identically.

Panels A and B put the same question to two scales and get opposite answers, and that disagreement is the result rather than a problem with it. Pooled across a season and with sequencing depth held equal, summer is the richer assemblage at every Hill order — 548 against winter's 383 OTUs at q = 0, and the gap widens under abundance weighting (412 vs 261 at q = 1; 287 vs 162 at q = 2). Within a single dropping the ordering reverses as soon as abundance enters: winter droppings are significantly more diverse at q = 1 (14.9 vs 7.4 effective OTUs; summer/winter 0.46, p = 0.001) and q = 2 (10.1 vs 4.6; 0.40, p < 0.001), whereas at q = 0 summer's higher mean (48.3 vs 31.3) is a weak, family-dependent difference carried by a few very rich summer samples (Tables S9, S9b). Panel C locates the reversal in dominance rather than in the species lists: an average summer sample gives 56% of its reads to a single OTU against 25% in winter, and Pielou evenness falls from 0.72 to 0.38 (both p \< 0.001). Summer droppings are far more top-heavy, which is precisely what depresses q = 1 and q = 2 even where a dropping's species list is as long as, or longer than, a winter one. Panel D names the taxa responsible, and they are the ones a coprophilous account predicts: *Thelebolus*, *Coniochaeta* and *Sporormiella intermedia* together take 44% of summer reads and are all dung saprotrophs, whereas winter's leading OTUs are mostly unclassified below class and carry no guild call at all — among them OTU1369, an unclassified Dothideomycete that is winter's most abundant OTU and is present in 20 of 26 winter samples, and which is taken up as a dark taxon in Section 3.4. Two caveats travel with the figure. The per-sample richness contrast in (B) is not robust to the choice of model family (Table S9b), so the crossover is firm at q = 1 and q = 2 and in the pooled estimates of (A), but not as a per-dropping richness gain. And the shares in (D) are seasonal averages, not universals — *Thelebolus* reaches its 24.9% mean while being detected in only 15 of the 26 summer droppings.

```{r fig4-build}
#| eval: false
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Full build code for Figure 4 — the source of truth for figures/main/Fig4_richness_evenness_crossover.{png,jpg,pdf}"

# Figure 4 -- Richness rises, evenness collapses (H2).
# Panels A and B share one grammar (Season on x, diversity on y, faceted by Hill
# order) and one set of facet strips, so the crossover is a single visual event:
# the same three columns, with the Winter->Summer slope flipping between rows.
# C then gives the mechanism (dominance) and D the identity of the dominants.
# Per-sample quantities are recomputed from the canonical objects (Fig. 1
# precedent) via the shared hill_size_helper.R; every pooled estimate and test
# statistic is READ from a committed tables/ CSV (Fig. 2 precedent), with guards
# asserting the two agree.
# Rebuild:  conda run -n r_env Rscript build_main_figure.R fig4-build

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(phyloseq); library(ggplot2); library(patchwork); library(iNEXT.3D)
})
# Size-standardised Hill numbers: the SAME single source the sec5-build chunk
# uses, so Figure 4 panel B and Section 5.2 cannot drift apart.
source("hill_size_helper.R")

rdata <- if (file.exists("eco_analysis.RData")) "eco_analysis.RData" else
         "/home/daniel/Ptarmigan/trimmed/mergedPlates/eco_analysis.RData"
load(rdata)
stopifnot(exists("alldat"), exists("alldat.rfy"), exists("alldat_full"),
          exists("funguild_otu"))                 # funguild_otu <- 8_functional_guilds.R
tab_dir <- if (dir.exists("tables")) "tables" else
           "/home/daniel/Ptarmigan/Scripts_server/Supplementary/tables"
out_dir <- "figures/main"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
grDevices::pdf(NULL)                                 # headless: no X11 fallback

# ---- shared style ----------------------------------------------------------
# Season and guild palettes are the repo standard (8_functional_guilds.R), so one
# colour means one thing across Fig. 1, Fig. 2 and Fig. 4.
season_cols  <- c(Winter = "#0072B2", Summer = "#D55E00")
guild_cols   <- c("Dung saprotroph" = "#E69F00", "Plant-associated" = "#009E73",
                  "Pathotroph" = "#CC79A7", "Other assigned" = "#56B4E9",
                  "Unassigned / dark" = "#999999")
GUILD_LEVELS <- names(guild_cols)

# The one facet vocabulary shared by panels A and B. A carries the strips; B
# repeats the columns beneath it and blanks them, exactly as Fig. 1B does.
Q_LEVELS <- c("q = 0  (richness)", "q = 1  (Shannon)", "q = 2  (Simpson)")

base_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.tag         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"),
        panel.spacing    = unit(0.8, "lines"),
        legend.key.size  = unit(0.42, "cm"),
        legend.title     = element_text(size = 10),
        legend.text      = element_text(size = 9))

# All in-plot text is ASCII. save_fig() falls back to grDevices::pdf when cairo
# is unavailable, and that device silently substitutes a dot for a Unicode minus
# or delta -- a corrupted PDF that would not fail the build.
pfmt <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "p = NA",
                    ifelse(p < 0.001, "p < 0.001", sprintf("p = %.3f", p)))
to_season <- function(x) factor(c(winter = "Winter", summer = "Summer")[as.character(x)],
                                levels = c("Winter", "Summer"))

# ============================================================================
# Panel A -- season-pool diversity (Section 5.1, Table S8)
# ============================================================================
# Read, never recomputed: 50 rarefaction draws x 100 bootstraps are expensive
# and the estimates are already committed. Pooling samples within a Season asks
# about the Season's whole species pool. These are the DEPTH-CONTROLLED,
# coverage-standardised estimates of Table S8 (every sample rarefied to 12,615
# reads, common coverage), not asymptotic ones: asymptotic richness extrapolates
# to ~2x observed here, and raw incidence carries summer's ~2.6x depth advantage.
asy <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "H2_iNEXT3D_TD_coverage_rarefied.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(setequal(asy$Season, c("Summer", "Winter")), setequal(asy$Order.q, 0:2))
asy$q      <- factor(Q_LEVELS[asy$Order.q + 1], levels = Q_LEVELS)
asy$Season <- factor(asy$Season, levels = c("Winter", "Summer"))
asy$TD_asy <- asy$qTD                                 # plotted estimate (name kept for the ggplot below)
sc_level   <- unique(asy$SC); stopifnot(length(sc_level) == 1L)

pick  <- function(sea) { d <- asy[asy$Season == sea, ]
                         d[match(Q_LEVELS, as.character(d$q)), ] }
A_sum <- pick("Summer"); A_win <- pick("Winter")
# The panel's whole claim in one line: summer above winter at every order, with
# 95% CIs that do not overlap. If that ever stops being true, the build stops.
stopifnot(all(A_sum$qTD.LCL > A_win$qTD.UCL))

pA <- ggplot(asy, aes(Season, TD_asy)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = 1), colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = qTD.LCL, ymax = qTD.UCL, colour = Season),
                width = 0.12, linewidth = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = Season), shape = 21, size = 3.4,
             colour = "grey25", stroke = 0.4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ q, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = season_cols) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = season_cols) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.18, 0.18))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Season pool\n(effective no. of OTUs)",
       subtitle = sprintf("Pooled-season diversity at equal depth (12,615 reads/sample) and equal coverage (%.2f); iNEXT3D, incidence,\nmedian over 50 rarefaction draws; bars are 95%% CIs. Summer exceeds winter at every order.", sc_level)) +
  base_theme +
  # A's x axis is identical to B's directly below, so only B prints it.
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank()) +
  guides(fill = "none", colour = "none")

# ============================================================================
# Panel B -- per-sample diversity (Section 5.2, Fig. S9 + Table S9)
# ============================================================================
# Raw counts: iNEXT.3D size-standardises internally to rfy_depth, the same depth
# alldat.rfy is rarefied to. Deterministic (an analytic expectation, not one
# rarefaction draw), so no seed is involved; the guard makes that testable.
ps_rfy <- alldat$nopool
m_rfy  <- as(otu_table(ps_rfy), "matrix")
if (taxa_are_rows(ps_rfy)) m_rfy <- t(m_rfy)         # sites x species
rfy_depth <- min(rowSums(m_rfy))
stopifnot(nsamples(ps_rfy) == 52L,
          rfy_depth == unique(rowSums(otu_mat_of(alldat.rfy$nopool))))

md_rfy <- data.frame(as(sample_data(ps_rfy), "data.frame"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(rownames(m_rfy), rownames(md_rfy)))
season_rfy <- to_season(md_rfy$Season); stopifnot(!anyNA(season_rfy))

hill_raw <- hill_inext_size(ps_rfy, level = rfy_depth, label = "Figure 4B")
stopifnot(identical(hill_raw$row, rownames(m_rfy)))
hill <- data.frame(Season = season_rfy,
                   q0 = hill_raw$q0, q1 = hill_raw$q1, q2 = hill_raw$q2)
hill_long <- data.frame(
  Season = rep(hill$Season, times = 3),
  q      = factor(rep(Q_LEVELS, each = nrow(hill)), levels = Q_LEVELS),
  value  = c(hill$q0, hill$q1, hill$q2))

# The annotated contrast is Table S9: a gamma GLM (log link, q ~ Season + Year)
# fitted to exactly the per-sample values plotted here (n = 52), so the figure
# and its test are on the same unit. Guards: the CSV's season means must equal
# the recomputed ones, and the model ratio must agree in direction with them.
lmm <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "H2_season_effect_per_sample.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(setequal(lmm$metric, c("q0", "q1", "q2")), all(lmm$n == nrow(hill)))
lmm <- lmm[match(c("q0", "q1", "q2"), lmm$metric), ]
obs_diff <- vapply(c("q0", "q1", "q2"), function(q)
  mean(hill[[q]][hill$Season == "Summer"]) - mean(hill[[q]][hill$Season == "Winter"]),
  numeric(1))
stopifnot(max(abs(lmm$mean_summer - lmm$mean_winter - obs_diff)) < 1e-8,
          all(sign(obs_diff) == sign(log(lmm$ratio_summer_winter))))

# Boxes show medians, but Section 5.3's text quotes MEANS -- so the means are
# drawn, and the segment joining them is what makes the slope flip legible
# against panel A directly above.
meanB <- aggregate(value ~ q + Season, hill_long, mean)
y_top <- as.numeric(tapply(hill_long$value, hill_long$q, max)[Q_LEVELS])
ann_B <- data.frame(q     = factor(Q_LEVELS, levels = Q_LEVELS),
                    value = y_top * 1.32,
                    lab   = sprintf("summer / winter\n%.2fx, %s",
                                    lmm$ratio_summer_winter, pfmt(lmm$p_season)))

# seed = on the jitter: save_fig() prints the object once per device, and an
# unseeded jitter would place the points differently in the PNG, the JPG and the
# PDF -- three subtly different figures from one build.
pB <- ggplot(hill_long, aes(Season, value)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = Season), outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.6, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.14, height = 0, seed = 1),
             size = 1.1, alpha = 0.55, colour = "grey20") +
  geom_line(data = meanB, aes(group = 1), colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(data = meanB, shape = 23, size = 2.4, stroke = 0.5,
             fill = "white", colour = "grey15") +
  geom_text(data = ann_B, aes(x = 1.5, label = lab), inherit.aes = TRUE,
            size = 2.9, lineheight = 0.95, vjust = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ q, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = season_cols) +
  # Linear, not log: a Hill number is an effective number of OTUs and is meant to
  # be read off the axis. free_y absorbs the 164-vs-32 range difference instead.
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.36))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Per sample\n(effective no. of OTUs)",
       subtitle = sprintf("Per-sample Hill numbers (n = %d, iNEXT3D size-standardised to %s reads); white diamonds are season means.\nAnnotations: year-adjusted summer/winter ratio, gamma GLM on these values (Table S9).",
                          nrow(hill), format(rfy_depth, big.mark = ","))) +
  base_theme +
  # B repeats A's facet columns exactly, so its strips are dropped as redundant.
  theme(strip.text = element_blank()) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1))

# ============================================================================
# Panel C -- dominance and evenness, the mechanism (Section 5.3, Table S10)
# ============================================================================
ps  <- alldat$nopool                                 # canonical, raw counts
m   <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
if (!taxa_are_rows(ps)) m <- t(m)                    # taxa x samples, as 5.3 uses
rel <- sweep(m, 2, colSums(m), "/")
stopifnot(all(abs(colSums(rel) - 1) < 1e-10))
md  <- data.frame(as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(colnames(rel), rownames(md)),
          setequal(colnames(rel), rownames(m_rfy)))  # B and C/D are the same 52 birds
season_c <- to_season(md$Season)

pielou_J <- function(p) { p <- p[p > 0]; -sum(p * log(p)) / log(length(p)) }
dom <- data.frame(Season    = season_c,
                  top1_prop = apply(rel, 2, max),
                  pielou_J  = apply(rel, 2, pielou_J))

# Drift guard: the recomputed means must reproduce committed Table S10 exactly at
# the precision the CSV stores (1 dp for the percentage, 2 dp for J).
dom_csv <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "report_dominance_summary.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
dom_csv <- dom_csv[match(c("winter", "summer"), dom_csv$Season), ]
obs_top1 <- tapply(dom$top1_prop, dom$Season, mean)
obs_J    <- tapply(dom$pielou_J,  dom$Season, mean)
stopifnot(max(abs(round(100 * as.numeric(obs_top1[c("Winter","Summer")]), 1) -
                  dom_csv$mean_top1_prop_pct)) < 1e-8,
          max(abs(round(as.numeric(obs_J[c("Winter","Summer")]), 2) -
                  dom_csv$mean_pielou_J)) < 1e-8)
p_top1 <- unique(dom_csv$wilcox_p_top1_prop); p_J <- unique(dom_csv$wilcox_p_pielou_J)
stopifnot(length(p_top1) == 1L, length(p_J) == 1L)

# Both metrics live on 0-1, so one shared axis works and the mechanism reads as a
# single picture: the seasons swap sides between the two metric groups.
# <br> not \n: these labels are rendered by element_markdown, which honours HTML
# breaks. Wrapped because the two names collide at this panel's width.
M_LEVELS <- c("Top-1 OTU<br>read share", "Pielou<br>evenness *J*")
dom_long <- data.frame(
  Season = rep(dom$Season, times = 2),
  Metric = factor(rep(M_LEVELS, each = nrow(dom)), levels = M_LEVELS),
  value  = c(dom$top1_prop, dom$pielou_J))
meanC <- aggregate(value ~ Metric + Season, dom_long, mean)
brk   <- data.frame(Metric = factor(M_LEVELS, levels = M_LEVELS),
                    lab    = pfmt(c(p_top1, p_J)),
                    xmid   = seq_along(M_LEVELS))
brk$xmin <- brk$xmid - 0.19; brk$xmax <- brk$xmid + 0.19  # dodge(0.75) box centres

pC <- ggplot(dom_long, aes(Metric, value, fill = Season)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.65, alpha = 0.85,
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.75)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.12, dodge.width = 0.75,
                                             seed = 1),
             size = 1.1, alpha = 0.55, colour = "grey20", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = meanC, aes(group = Season), inherit.aes = TRUE,
             position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), shape = 23, size = 2.3,
             stroke = 0.5, fill = "white", colour = "grey15", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_segment(data = brk, aes(x = xmin, xend = xmax, y = 1.03, yend = 1.03),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(data = brk, aes(x = xmid, y = 1.055, label = lab), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            size = 3, vjust = 0) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = season_cols) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.13), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Per-sample value (proportion)",
       subtitle = "White diamonds are season means;\nbrackets give the Wilcoxon rank-sum test (Table S10).") +
  base_theme +
  # The x labels carry markdown (*J*); without element_markdown the asterisks
  # print literally, and this theme() must come after base_theme to win.
  theme(axis.text.x = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 9)) +
  guides(fill = "none")

# ============================================================================
# Panel D -- who the dominants are (Section 5.4, Table S11), by guild
# ============================================================================
top5 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(season_c), function(s) {
  cols   <- colnames(rel)[season_c == s]
  shares <- rowMeans(rel[, cols, drop = FALSE])      # mean WITHIN-season share
  ids    <- names(sort(shares, decreasing = TRUE))[1:5]
  data.frame(Season = s, OTU = ids, share = 100 * shares[ids],
             n_detect = rowSums(rel[ids, cols, drop = FALSE] > 0),
             n_season = length(cols), stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}))
top5$Season <- factor(top5$Season, levels = c("Winter", "Summer"))

# Drift guard: same OTUs, same order, same shares as committed Table S11.
t5_csv <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "report_top5_otu_by_season.csv"),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
t5_csv$Season <- to_season(t5_csv$Season)
t5_csv <- t5_csv[order(t5_csv$Season, -t5_csv$mean_pct_share), ]
chk    <- top5[order(top5$Season, -top5$share), ]
stopifnot(identical(paste(chk$Season, chk$OTU), paste(t5_csv$Season, t5_csv$OTU)),
          max(abs(round(chk$share, 2) - t5_csv$mean_pct_share)) < 1e-8)

# UNITE taxonomy carries rank prefixes ("g__Thelebolus") and, at species level, a
# trailing hypothesis index ("intermedia 1"). Labels fall back down the ranks
# until something is assigned: a family name stands alone unambiguously, an order
# or class does not and is prefixed "unclassified". Markdown asterisks italicise
# real Latin names only -- never a rank name, never an Incertae sedis placeholder.
tax <- data.frame(as(tax_table(ps), "matrix"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
strip_rank <- function(x) sub("^[a-z]__", "", x)
clean_rank <- function(x) { x <- strip_rank(x)
  x[is.na(x) | x == "" | x == "NA" | grepl("unidentified", x, ignore.case = TRUE)] <- NA_character_
  x }
otu_label <- function(otu) {
  rk <- lapply(c("Genus", "Species", "Family", "Order", "Class"),
               function(r) clean_rank(tax[otu, r]))
  names(rk) <- c("Genus", "Species", "Family", "Order", "Class")
  incertae <- function(x) !is.na(x) && grepl("Incertae_sedis", x)
  nm <-
    if (!is.na(rk$Genus) && !incertae(rk$Genus)) {
      if (!is.na(rk$Species))
        paste0("*", rk$Genus, " ", sub("[ _]+[0-9]+$", "", rk$Species), "*")
      else paste0("*", rk$Genus, "*")
    } else if (incertae(rk$Genus))                      sub("_gen_Incertae_sedis", " (unclass.)", rk$Genus)
      else if (!is.na(rk$Family) && !incertae(rk$Family)) rk$Family
      else if (!is.na(rk$Order))                        paste("unclassified", rk$Order)
      else if (!is.na(rk$Class))                        paste("unclassified", rk$Class)
      else                                              "unclassified fungus"
  paste0(nm, " (", otu, ")")
}
top5$label <- unname(vapply(top5$OTU, otu_label, character(1)))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(top5$label))

# Guild rule VERBATIM from the Fig. 1 chunk (itself from 8_functional_guilds.R),
# including its genus cleaning, so Fig. 1, Fig. 4, Section 8 and Section 9 all
# classify an OTU identically. One consequence is visible here: FUNGuild returns
# a compound string for Candida parapsilosis containing "Epiphyte", so the
# priority rule lands OTU136 in Plant-associated. That is an artifact of compound
# FUNGuild strings, not a claim about the taxon -- but the rule is applied
# unchanged rather than special-cased, because cross-section consistency is worth
# more than one prettier label.
COPRO_GENERA <- c("Sordaria","Podospora","Cercophora","Chaetomium","Schizothecium",
                  "Preussia","Delitschia","Pilobolus","Ascobolus","Saccobolus",
                  "Sporormiella","Coprinopsis","Thelebolus","Coniochaeta")
gen       <- strip_rank(tax$Genus[match(top5$OTU, rownames(tax))])
gen       <- ifelse(gen %in% c("", "NA"), NA, gen)
guild_str <- funguild_otu$Guild[match(top5$OTU, funguild_otu$OTU_ID)]
is_copro  <- (!is.na(guild_str) & grepl("Dung Saprotroph", guild_str)) |
             (!is.na(gen)       & gen %in% COPRO_GENERA)
is_plant  <- !is_copro & !is.na(guild_str) &
             grepl("Endophyte|Plant Saprotroph|Plant Pathogen|Epiphyte", guild_str)
is_patho  <- !is_copro & !is_plant & !is.na(guild_str) & grepl("Pathogen|Parasite", guild_str)
top5$Guild <- factor(
  ifelse(is_copro, "Dung saprotroph",
  ifelse(is_plant, "Plant-associated",
  ifelse(is_patho, "Pathotroph",
  ifelse(!is.na(guild_str), "Other assigned", "Unassigned / dark")))),
  levels = GUILD_LEVELS)

# The two seasons' top-5 sets are disjoint, so one global factor ordered
# (Season, share) gives each facet its own descending bars under free_y.
top5 <- top5[order(top5$Season, top5$share), ]
top5$label <- factor(top5$label, levels = top5$label)
n_lab <- setNames(sprintf("%s (n = %d)", levels(season_c), as.integer(table(season_c))),
                  levels(season_c))

pD <- ggplot(top5, aes(share, label, fill = Guild)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%  (%d/%d)", share, n_detect, n_season)),
            hjust = -0.12, size = 2.8, colour = "grey25") +
  facet_grid(Season ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y",
             labeller = labeller(Season = n_lab)) +
  # drop = TRUE: "Other assigned" has no member among these ten OTUs and a key
  # with no bar is noise; the level ORDER stays the repo-canonical one.
  scale_fill_manual(values = guild_cols, name = "Functional guild", drop = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.32))) +
  labs(x = "Mean within-season read share (%)", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "Bar labels give the mean share and, in parentheses,\nthe number of that season's samples with any detection.") +
  base_theme +
  theme(axis.text.y = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 9)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 2, nrow = 2))

# ---- assemble and write ----------------------------------------------------
# An explicit design grid, not nested `/` and `|`: patchwork FLATTENS a chain of
# `/`, so (pA / pB) / (pC | pD) silently becomes a three-row layout and errors.
# The grid also guarantees what panel A and B depend on -- one shared column
# geometry, so their facet columns line up and the slope flip reads vertically.
# D gets five of the eight columns because its taxon labels are up to 38 chars.
design <- "
AAAAAAAA
BBBBBBBB
CCCDDDDD
"
fig4 <- pA + pB + pC + pD +
  plot_layout(design = design, heights = c(1, 1.18, 1.55), guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "horizontal")

# Every main figure is written three ways: PNG and JPG (600 dpi raster, for
# submission systems that demand one or the other) and PDF (vector, for print).
save_fig <- function(stem, obj, width, height, res = 600) {
  one <- function(open_dev) { open_dev(); on.exit(grDevices::dev.off()); print(obj) }
  one(function() grDevices::png(paste0(stem, ".png"), width = width, height = height,
                                units = "in", res = res))
  one(function() grDevices::jpeg(paste0(stem, ".jpg"), width = width, height = height,
                                 units = "in", res = res, quality = 95))
  pdf_dev <- if (capabilities("cairo")) grDevices::cairo_pdf else grDevices::pdf
  one(function() pdf_dev(paste0(stem, ".pdf"), width = width, height = height))
}
save_fig(file.path(out_dir, "Fig4_richness_evenness_crossover"), fig4, 10, 10.4)

# ---- console summary -------------------------------------------------------
cat("Season-pool diversity, depth-controlled and coverage-standardised (Table S8):\n")
print(data.frame(q = Q_LEVELS,
                 summer = sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", A_sum$TD_asy, A_sum$qTD.LCL, A_sum$qTD.UCL),
                 winter = sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", A_win$TD_asy, A_win$qTD.LCL, A_win$qTD.UCL)),
      row.names = FALSE)
hill_means <- aggregate(cbind(q0, q1, q2) ~ Season, hill, mean)
hill_means[-1] <- round(hill_means[-1], 2)
cat(sprintf("\nPer-sample Hill means (n = %d, size-standardised to %d reads):\n", nrow(hill), rfy_depth))
print(hill_means, row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nPer-sample gamma GLM, summer/winter ratio (n = 52; Table S9):\n")
print(data.frame(metric = lmm$metric, ratio = round(lmm$ratio_summer_winter, 3),
                 lwr = round(lmm$ratio_lwr, 3), upr = round(lmm$ratio_upr, 3),
                 p = signif(lmm$p_season, 3)), row.names = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("\nTop-1 OTU read share: summer %.1f%% vs winter %.1f%%  (%s)\n",
            100 * obs_top1[["Summer"]], 100 * obs_top1[["Winter"]], pfmt(p_top1)))
cat(sprintf("Pielou evenness J   : summer %.2f  vs winter %.2f   (%s)\n",
            obs_J[["Summer"]], obs_J[["Winter"]], pfmt(p_J)))
cat("\nTop-5 OTUs per season (mean within-season read share):\n")
print(data.frame(Season = chk$Season, OTU = chk$OTU, share_pct = round(chk$share, 2),
                 detected = sprintf("%d/%d", chk$n_detect, chk$n_season),
                 guild = as.character(top5$Guild[match(chk$OTU, top5$OTU)])),
      row.names = FALSE)
```

### 10.5 Figure 5 — Dark, largely novel lineages dominate winter dung (E1)

:::: {.content-visible when-profile="docs"}
*Provenance: all three panels come from Section 3.4. Fig. 5A is the main-text version of Figure S-E1b, with the last two placement categories merged; Fig. 5B is built from `tables/E1_SH_readshare_by_sample.csv`, written by `9_dark_taxa_SH_matching.R` Section 4b; Fig. 5C plots Table S-E1b. Every value is read from the committed `tables/` CSVs written by `9_dark_taxa_SH_matching.R` — nothing is recomputed from sequence data, because the Species Hypothesis assignment is an external pipeline step (a containerised run of the TU-NHM `sh_matching` workflow against the UNITE reference). The best-hit similarity histogram that was Fig. 5A in an earlier version is now supplementary only (Figure S-E1a).*
::::

![](figures/main/Fig5_dark_taxa_SH.png)

**Figure 5**: Winter dung is dominated by fungal lineages that carry no confident genus, and most of that fraction is not merely unnamed but absent from the reference database. **(A)** UNITE Species Hypothesis placement of all 493 dark OTUs — those the naïve-Bayes classifier leaves without a confident genus. The second and third categories are the same kind of outcome: neither falls inside an existing named Species Hypothesis, and they differ only in whether the sequence has any UNITE relative at all. "Candidate novel SH" has one (median best hit 92.0% identity across these 228 OTUs) and so inherits a partial lineage from its neighbours; "no reference within 80% id" has none, and additionally absorbs 13 OTUs that the pipeline filtered before the matching step. Together they are 331 of the 493 dark OTUs (67%). **(B)** Mean per-sample read share of the same categories, by season, with the named fraction added to reach 100% of reads (52 droppings, 26 per season; segments below 5% are unlabelled). This is the read-weighted counterpart to (A): counting OTUs says nothing about how much of a dropping they are. Candidate-novel lineages hold 29% of winter reads against 7% of summer reads (Wilcoxon *p* = 1.9 × 10⁻⁵), and the dark fraction as a whole is 51% of winter against 31% of summer reads. **(C)** The 30 dark OTUs with the highest mean winter read share (Table S-E1b), plotted as prevalence — the number of the 26 winter samples with any detection — against that mean share, coloured as in (A). OTU1369 is labelled: it is winter's single most abundant OTU at 11.2% of winter reads and is present in 20 of 26 winter droppings, yet its best UNITE hit is only 85% similar, so it forms a candidate new Species Hypothesis rather than matching anything named.

Roughly half of a typical winter dropping is reads that the canonical taxonomy cannot name (Section 3.4), and that single label covers two different problems. A little over a third of dark OTUs are near-identical to a UNITE reference and are dark only because `minBoot = 80` declines to commit to a genus at that bootstrap — a cost of conservatism, and one that Species Hypothesis matching largely recovers (of the 390 dark OTUs with a best hit at all, 37% sit at ≥ 99% identity; Figure S-E1a). But a comparable fraction of them (38%) sits below 95% identity, where no threshold adjustment would help, and panel A shows where that leads: 228 of the 493 dark OTUs (46%) form candidate new Species Hypotheses rather than matching an existing one, and a further 103 (21%) have no UNITE reference within 80% identity at all. Two thirds of the unnamed community is therefore unnamed because the reference lacks it, not because the classifier was cautious. Panel B supplies the weight behind that count, and it is strongly seasonal: candidate-novel lineages account for 29% of winter reads but only 7% of summer reads, so winter dung is not merely more dark than summer dung, it is dark in a different way — dominated by lineages with no named counterpart rather than by unnamed relatives of known ones. Panel C locates that signal in individual taxa: the dark OTUs carrying real winter read share are predominantly candidate-novel, and the most extreme of them, OTU1369, is simultaneously the most abundant and among the most prevalent OTUs in winter dung while being only 85% similar to its nearest named relative. One caveat travels with the figure throughout. "Candidate novel" is a statement about the reference database rather than a taxonomic claim: these are unimprinted clusters awaiting public sequence deposition and PlutoF registration (Section 3.4), so none of them yet carries a permanent identifier.

```{r fig5-build}
#| eval: false
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Full build code for Figure 5 — the source of truth for figures/main/Fig5_dark_taxa_SH.{png,jpg,pdf}"

# Figure 5 -- Winter dung is dominated by unclassified, largely candidate-novel
# lineages (E1). Every quantity here is READ from committed tables/ CSVs written
# by 9_dark_taxa_SH_matching.R; nothing is recomputed from sequence data, because
# the SH assignment itself is the expensive external step (a Singularity run of
# the TU-NHM sh_matching pipeline against the UNITE reference, ~90 min).
#   A  tables/E1_SH_assignment_summary.csv     (the 493 dark OTUs' placement)
#   B  tables/E1_SH_readshare_by_sample.csv    (script 9 Section 4b, 52 samples)
#   C  tables/E1_winter_dominant_dark_taxa_SH.csv (top 30 by winter read share)
# tables/dark_taxa_SH_matching.csv is the per-OTU table all three are derived
# from; it is read here purely as a drift guard on A and C.
# Rebuild:  conda run -n r_env Rscript build_main_figure.R fig5-build

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2); library(patchwork)
})

tab_dir <- if (dir.exists("tables")) "tables" else
           "/home/daniel/Ptarmigan/Scripts_server/Supplementary/tables"
out_dir <- "figures/main"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
grDevices::pdf(NULL)                                 # headless: no X11 fallback

# ---- shared style ----------------------------------------------------------
# ONE colour dimension across all three panels, so every coloured mark in the
# figure means exactly one thing. Panels A and C show dark OTUs only and use the
# last three levels; panel B adds the named fraction to reach 100% of reads.
#
# "Candidate novel SH" and "No reference within 80% id" are the SAME kind of
# outcome -- neither falls inside an existing named SH -- and differ only in
# whether the sequence has any UNITE relative at all. The palette says so: the
# third level is a lightness tint of the second rather than an unrelated hue.
# (Lightness contrast survives every form of colour-vision deficiency, so the
# pair stays separable while still reading as one family.)
STRAT_LEVELS <- c("Named (genus assigned)", "Placeable to existing SH",
                  "Candidate novel SH", "No reference within 80% id")
strat_cols <- c("Named (genus assigned)"     = "#B8B8B8",   # not a dark OTU
                "Placeable to existing SH"   = "#0072B2",   # resolved
                "Candidate novel SH"         = "#D55E00",   # the novel signal
                "No reference within 80% id" = "#E8A87C")   # novel, no relative
SH_LEVELS <- STRAT_LEVELS[-1]                        # the dark-OTU categories

base_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.tag         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"),
        panel.spacing    = unit(0.8, "lines"),
        legend.key.size  = unit(0.42, "cm"),
        legend.title     = element_text(size = 10),
        legend.text      = element_text(size = 9))

# One scale object reused by all three panels: patchwork can only collect guides
# that are identical, so `limits` (not the data) fixes the key order everywhere.
fill_scale <- scale_fill_manual(values = strat_cols, name = "Taxonomy / SH placement",
                                limits = STRAT_LEVELS, drop = FALSE)

# All in-plot text is ASCII: save_fig() falls back to grDevices::pdf when cairo is
# unavailable, and that device silently substitutes a dot for a Unicode glyph.
# no_SH_match and excluded_nonITS collapse into one displayed category -- see the
# caption; Section 3.4 keeps them separate.
sh_class_map <- c(placeable_existing_SH = "Placeable to existing SH",
                  novel_new_SH          = "Candidate novel SH",
                  no_SH_match           = "No reference within 80% id",
                  excluded_nonITS       = "No reference within 80% id")

# ============================================================================
# Panel A -- where the 493 dark OTUs land
# ============================================================================
sh <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "dark_taxa_SH_matching.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(is.logical(sh$is_dark), !anyNA(sh$is_dark), nrow(sh) == 1129L,
          all(sh$SH_class %in% names(sh_class_map)))

asum <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "E1_SH_assignment_summary.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(asum) == 1L)

# Tabulated from the per-OTU table rather than read off the summary's four
# fields, because two of those fields now collapse into one displayed bar.
dark_cat <- factor(unname(sh_class_map[sh$SH_class[sh$is_dark]]), levels = SH_LEVELS)
bdf <- data.frame(cat = factor(SH_LEVELS, levels = SH_LEVELS),
                  n   = as.integer(table(dark_cat)[SH_LEVELS]))
# Drift guard: the committed summary must still agree with the per-OTU table,
# both in total and in the merge that produces the third bar.
stopifnot(asum$n_dark == sum(sh$is_dark), sum(bdf$n) == asum$n_dark,
          sum(asum$placeable_existing_SH, asum$novel_new_SH,
              asum$no_SH_match, asum$excluded_nonITS) == asum$n_dark,
          bdf$n[3] == asum$no_SH_match + asum$excluded_nonITS)
bdf$pct <- 100 * bdf$n / asum$n_dark
bdf$cat <- factor(bdf$cat, levels = rev(SH_LEVELS))   # first category at the top

pA <- ggplot(bdf, aes(n, cat, fill = cat)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.68, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%d  (%.0f%%)", n, pct)), hjust = -0.12,
            size = 3.1, colour = "grey25") +
  fill_scale +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.42))) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) sub(" (to existing SH|within 80% id)",
                                            "\n\\1", x)) +
  labs(x = sprintf("Dark OTUs (n = %d)", asum$n_dark), y = NULL,
       subtitle = "Every OTU with no\nconfident genus\nassignment.") +
  base_theme +
  guides(fill = "none")

# ============================================================================
# Panel B -- how much of a dropping each stratum accounts for, by season
# ============================================================================
# Panel A counts OTUs, which says nothing about how much of the community they
# are; this panel is the read-weighted view and the one that carries the
# figure's claim. Written per sample by 9_dark_taxa_SH_matching.R Section 4b, so
# the mean and the test below come from the same committed file.
rs <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "E1_SH_readshare_by_sample.csv"),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
rs_map <- c("Named"                   = "Named (genus assigned)",
            "Dark: placeable"         = "Placeable to existing SH",
            "Dark: candidate novel"   = "Candidate novel SH",
            "Dark: no reference <80%" = "No reference within 80% id")
stopifnot(all(rs$stratum %in% names(rs_map)), all(rs$Season %in% c("winter", "summer")))
rs$cat <- factor(unname(rs_map[rs$stratum]), levels = STRAT_LEVELS)
# Compositional guard: the four strata must exhaust each sample's reads.
stopifnot(abs(tapply(rs$read_share, rs$sample, sum) - 1) < 1e-6,
          length(unique(rs$sample)) == 52L)

# Season is capitalised for display only; winter first because the figure's
# subject is the winter community.
rs$Season <- factor(sub("^(.)", "\\U\\1", rs$Season, perl = TRUE),
                    levels = c("Winter", "Summer"))
bar <- aggregate(read_share ~ Season + cat, data = rs, FUN = mean)
bar$pct <- 100 * bar$read_share
bar <- bar[order(bar$Season, bar$cat), ]
# Label positions are computed here rather than left to position_stack. The text
# layer plots a SUBSET (segments too thin to hold a label), and position_stack
# re-stacks whatever data it is given -- so the two layers would silently drift
# apart in any season where a segment is dropped. geom_col stacks the first
# factor level on top, hence the descending cumulative.
bar$ymid <- unlist(lapply(split(bar$pct, bar$Season), function(v)
  (sum(v) - cumsum(c(0, head(v, -1)))) - v / 2))
# Drift guard: these means must reproduce the per-OTU table's season columns,
# which are computed independently (script 9 Section 4, not 4b).
chk <- vapply(split(seq_len(nrow(sh)), factor(
                ifelse(sh$is_dark, unname(sh_class_map[sh$SH_class]),
                       "Named (genus assigned)"), levels = STRAT_LEVELS)),
              function(i) sum(sh$winter_mean_share[i]), numeric(1))
win <- setNames(bar$read_share[bar$Season == "Winter"],
                as.character(bar$cat[bar$Season == "Winter"]))
stopifnot(max(abs(chk[STRAT_LEVELS] - win[STRAT_LEVELS])) < 1e-6)

nov <- rs[rs$cat == "Candidate novel SH", ]
nov_p <- wilcox.test(read_share ~ Season, data = nov)$p.value
nov_m <- tapply(100 * nov$read_share, nov$Season, mean)

pB <- ggplot(bar, aes(Season, pct, fill = cat)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.62, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.15) +
  # Labelled inside the segment it belongs to; segments under 5% have no room,
  # and the axis already places them.
  geom_text(data = bar[bar$pct >= 5, ],
            aes(y = ymid, label = sprintf("%.0f%%", pct),
                colour = cat == "Candidate novel SH"),
            size = 3.0, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "grey20")) +
  fill_scale +
  # coord_cartesian, not scale limits: position_stack sums to 1 and the scale is
  # applied AFTER stacking, so a limit of exactly 100 drops the top segment on a
  # floating-point overshoot (ggplot2 4.0 warns "Removed 1 row").
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean per-sample read share (%)",
       subtitle = sprintf("Mean per-sample read share.\nCandidate-novel: %.0f%% winter vs\n%.0f%% summer (p = %s).",
                          nov_m[["Winter"]], nov_m[["Summer"]],
                          format(signif(nov_p, 2), scientific = TRUE))) +
  base_theme +
  # The figure's one legend lives here: panel B is the only one that carries all
  # four levels, and its geom_col draws square keys, which read correctly for
  # both the bars here and the points in C. A and C suppress theirs.
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1, nrow = 1))

# ============================================================================
# Panel C -- the winter-abundant dark OTUs
# ============================================================================
# The committed top-30-by-winter-read-share table, so the panel's membership is a
# published definition rather than a threshold invented for the figure.
wd <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "E1_winter_dominant_dark_taxa_SH.csv"),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(wd) == 30L, all(wd$winter_n == 26L), all(wd$OTU_ID %in% sh$OTU_ID))
wd$cat <- factor(unname(sh_class_map[wd$SH_class]), levels = SH_LEVELS)
wd$share_pct <- 100 * wd$winter_mean_share
# Drift guard: this table must be the top 30 of the per-OTU table it came from.
top30 <- sh$OTU_ID[sh$is_dark][order(-sh$winter_mean_share[sh$is_dark])][1:30]
stopifnot(setequal(wd$OTU_ID, top30))

lab <- wd[wd$OTU_ID == "OTU1369", ]
stopifnot(nrow(lab) == 1L, lab$winter_occ == 20L)     # agrees with Fig. 4D
lab$txt <- sprintf("OTU1369\ncandidate novel SH, %.0f%% id\n%.1f%% of winter reads, %d/%d samples",
                   lab$similarity_percentage, lab$share_pct, lab$winter_occ, lab$winter_n)

pC <- ggplot(wd, aes(winter_occ, share_pct, fill = cat)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 3.2, colour = "grey25", stroke = 0.4, alpha = 0.9) +
  # Hung below-left of the marker rather than centred on it, so the point stays
  # visibly a data point instead of reading as punctuation inside the text.
  geom_text(data = lab, aes(label = txt), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            x = lab$winter_occ - 0.8, y = lab$share_pct - 0.7, hjust = 1, vjust = 1,
            size = 2.9, lineheight = 1.05, colour = "grey20") +
  fill_scale +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 26), breaks = seq(0, 25, 5),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.02))) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.10))) +
  labs(x = sprintf("Prevalence (of %d winter samples)", wd$winter_n[1]),
       y = "Mean winter read share (%)",
       subtitle = "The 30 dark OTUs with the\nhighest mean winter read\nshare (Table S-E1b).") +
  base_theme +
  guides(fill = "none")

# ---- assemble and write ----------------------------------------------------
# Explicit widths rather than nested `/` and `|`: patchwork FLATTENS a chain of
# `/`, so a mixed layout can silently become extra rows.
fig5 <- pA + pB + pC +
  plot_layout(nrow = 1, widths = c(1.1, 0.75, 1.5), guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "horizontal")

# Every main figure is written three ways: PNG and JPG (600 dpi raster, for
# submission systems that demand one or the other) and PDF (vector, for print).
save_fig <- function(stem, obj, width, height, res = 600) {
  one <- function(open_dev) { open_dev(); on.exit(grDevices::dev.off()); print(obj) }
  one(function() grDevices::png(paste0(stem, ".png"), width = width, height = height,
                                units = "in", res = res))
  one(function() grDevices::jpeg(paste0(stem, ".jpg"), width = width, height = height,
                                 units = "in", res = res, quality = 95))
  pdf_dev <- if (capabilities("cairo")) grDevices::cairo_pdf else grDevices::pdf
  one(function() pdf_dev(paste0(stem, ".pdf"), width = width, height = height))
}
save_fig(file.path(out_dir, "Fig5_dark_taxa_SH"), fig5, 10, 5.0)

# ---- console summary -------------------------------------------------------
cat(sprintf("Dark OTUs (n = %d) by SH placement:\n", asum$n_dark))
print(data.frame(placement = SH_LEVELS,
                 n = bdf$n[match(SH_LEVELS, as.character(bdf$cat))],
                 pct = round(bdf$pct[match(SH_LEVELS, as.character(bdf$cat))], 1)),
      row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nMean per-sample read share (%), by season:\n")
print(round(100 * xtabs(read_share ~ cat + Season, data = bar), 2))
cat(sprintf("\nCandidate-novel read share: winter %.1f%% vs summer %.1f%%, Wilcoxon p = %.3g\n",
            nov_m[["Winter"]], nov_m[["Summer"]], nov_p))
cat("\nTop 10 winter-abundant dark OTUs:\n")
o <- order(-wd$share_pct)[1:10]
print(data.frame(OTU = wd$OTU_ID[o], class = sub("^c__", "", wd$Class[o]),
                 winter_pct = round(wd$share_pct[o], 2),
                 prevalence = sprintf("%d/%d", wd$winter_occ[o], wd$winter_n[o]),
                 id = wd$similarity_percentage[o],
                 placement = as.character(wd$cat[o])), row.names = FALSE)
```
